final_message:
I've built the June recap workbook. In June, 48 POs across 7 accounts shipped **$140,008.20 at cost** against $145,218.80 ordered on those POs. That's 96.4% shipped and **$5,210.60 short-shipped**. Another 5 POs had a full June ship window but slipped to July, worth **$13,300.00 at cost**.

I checked the totals in Python. No spreadsheet program was available here to recalculate the Excel formulas, so they will calculate when the file is first opened in Excel.

**Table 1 – June shipped, by account (ship date 6/1–6/30/25)**

| Account | POs | Order $ cost | Shipped $ cost | % shipped | $ short |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dolce | 2 | 10,766.40 | 10,443.41 | 97.0% | 322.99 |
| Five O Fore | 8 | 25,766.00 | 24,993.02 | 97.0% | 772.98 |
| Hunt's | 7 | 15,451.40 | 15,439.40 | 99.9% | 12.00 |
| Marchand | 9 | 27,081.00 | 26,883.29 | 99.3% | 197.71 |
| Pronto | 8 | 18,903.00 | 18,794.44 | 99.4% | 108.56 |
| Sigma | 8 | 22,687.60 | 21,154.29 | 93.2% | 1,533.31 |
| Thread Up | 6 | 24,563.40 | 22,300.35 | 90.8% | 2,263.05 |

Thread Up and Sigma account for most of the short-shipped dollars.

**Table 2 – June-window POs that shipped in July:**
- **The 5 POs:** Marchand $4,700 (2 POs), Thread Up $3,900, Sigma $2,600 and Pronto $2,100.
- **Already shipped:** all five went out on 7/1, for $13,248.00 at cost.
- **June impact:** if they had shipped on time, June would have been $153,256.20, or 9.5% higher.
- **Past cancel:** all five shipped 1–4 days after their cancel date, so the account managers should confirm the customers accepted them and won't charge back.

**About the June number:** it includes 20 POs that shipped outside their ship window. Each one is marked on the PO detail tab:
- 9 POs from May windows that shipped 6/2, after their cancel dates ($26,530.83).
- 4 June-window POs that shipped late ($10,594.00).
- 7 POs that shipped before their start date ($17,803.00). Four of these had windows running into July.

I counted them all as June shipments because the rule is based only on the actual ship date.

**Assumptions** (also written into the workbook):
- No registry or operations records were included, only the PO Log. I treated it as the operative record.
- All values are at cost, and I treated the June fiscal month as 6/1–6/30.
- For Table 2 I used the rule as you gave it: start and cancel dates both in June. Another 11 POs started in June but had July cancel dates and shipped in July ($30,334.40). I left them out because they were still within their window, and noted them on the sheet.

The workbook also has a recap tab with the summary sentences, a tab for each table, a PO detail tab and a copy of the source log. Every table has an account filter, and the totals rows update to match whatever is filtered.

DONE
